summary: Backend-only test of the MetaApi ReadTimeout resilience fix, run against the MetaApi mock :8012 with fault injection while the forex market was open. Base suite test_iter34 passed 15/15. New suite test_iter35_metaapi_resilience_extra.py passed 12/13. It covers: 429 with recommendedRetryTime retried on GETs and not on trades, 503 retried on GETs while a trade 503 is 'unknown', a trade ReadTimeout sent once as 'unknown', 404 NotSynchronized treated as transient, 404 not-found treated as rejected, a clear 401 token message, _retry_after clamped to 0.5–30 s, and the default of 180. At engine level it covers: an INVALID_STOPS rejection logged once and immediately as 'orden REAL rechazada' with a signal note and no position; trade disabled; a manual close POST /positions/{id}/close with a transient fault giving 'cierre REAL ejecutado en el intento 2'; DISCONNECTED_DURING_TRADE when the order was not executed, retried without a duplicate; and close-all during a persistent outage, which returned {closed:0, failed:1}, kept the position and closed it later. Regressions passed: iter18+iter32+iter33 27/27 and iter21 10/10. One real edge-case bug was found (see rca). The backend works and all requested scenarios behave as specified.

critical.issue: If a trade returns 'unknown' (HTTP ReadTimeout, which is the user's exact scenario) and the clientId lookup's GET /positions then also fails (MetaApi slow or unreachable), the MetaApiError(kind='transient') raised inside on_unknown() propagates unchanged. The engine then logs 'orden REAL no enviada · … · verificado: no quedó ninguna orden abierta' and drops the signal, but the order DID execute at the broker. The result is an untracked orphan position: it has SL/TP but no bot management (trailing, expiry, PnL), and the log line is false. Reproduced in test_iter35::TestReconcileEdge: the mock had 1 new position, and the error was kind=transient, attempts=4, 'MetaApi no responde: ReadTimeout'.

minor.issue: On first boot load() inserts the full FxConfig().model_dump(), so every existing install (including the user's VPS) already has hfm_alert_after_sec=60 stored. Changing the default to 180 only affects new installs. A one-off migration is needed (60 → 180 when the user never changed it). In the preview DB the stored value was 60; the tester set it to 180.
When a GET runs out of retries on a 429, err.attempts is not set and stays at 1 instead of 4. This only affects reporting.
Non-MetaApi exceptions (e.g. the ValueError for a lot below the broker minimum) are still logged as 'orden REAL rechazada por HFM/MetaApi', which is misleading. Pre-existing.
There is no adoption of broker positions that carry an AIT_*_o clientId but have no DB record. Such positions are never synced into the bot, which makes the HIGH issue worse.

action_items: HIGH: in FxLiveBroker._with_retries, wrap on_unknown() in try/except MetaApiError. If the reconcile itself fails, re-raise with kind='unknown' (do not retry, do not create a new link). In engine.open_position, handle kind=='unknown' separately: log RISK 'resultado desconocido · se verificará', and either schedule a background reconcile by link_id that adopts the position into the DB when found, or at least never claim 'verificado: no quedó ninguna orden abierta'.
Consider periodic adoption (in the HFM sync loop) of broker positions with an AIT_[0-9a-f]{8}_o clientId/magic 777001 that have no DB record.
Migrate stored hfm_alert_after_sec=60 → 180 on load (e.g. an applied-default version flag), otherwise existing users keep the 60 s alert.
Minor: set err.attempts on the 429 exhaustion path in MetaApi._call; label non-MetaApi exceptions in open_position as 'orden REAL no enviada' instead of 'rechazada por HFM/MetaApi'.
critical_code_review_comments: _with_retries: an exception from on_unknown escapes the unknown→transient conversion logic and reports a false 'verified' result (see HIGH issue).

find_position_by_client_id: 6 tries × 2.5 s plus the order-history lookup gives about 13–15 s of reconcile per unknown result. A large read_timeout (20 s × 4 attempts per GET) can stretch this to minutes while the engine lock is held.
engine.py is 852 lines; the file should be split (open/close live logic into its own module).
Classification sets are disjoint (verified), OK_CODES include the MT4 ERR_NO_ERROR and TRADE_RETCODE_NO_CHANGES, and the clientId format AIT_<8hex>_o/_c is ≤31 chars (verified).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Run with -n 0. test_iter35::TestReconcileEdge::test_unknown_then_reconcile_reads_fail is expected to FAIL until the HIGH fix lands. It uses FxLiveBroker with trade_timeout=1.5 and read_timeout=0.5 plus fault(trade_hang=3, times=1, positions_hang=3, positions_times=100). The crypto bot was running in PAPER and was not touched; its status endpoint is GET /api/ (GET /api/status returns 404). FX ended in PAPER, stopped, with no HFM config.
rca of the issue: Repro: the order is executed at the broker, but the HTTP response times out, so trade() raises kind='unknown'. _with_retries calls on_unknown() → _reconcile_open() → api.find_position_by_client_id() → api.positions() → _call GET times out 4 times and raises MetaApiError(kind='transient'). That exception escapes from inside the except-block of _with_retries without being re-classified. engine.open_position receives kind=='transient' and logs 'orden REAL no enviada … verificado: no quedó ninguna orden abierta'. Expected: kind='unknown' / an 'unverified' status and a later reconcile. Observed: transient with a false 'verified', and an untracked broker position. Mitigation: catch reconcile errors and keep kind='unknown', stop retrying (to avoid duplicates), surface a distinct log and Telegram message, and adopt the position later by clientId.
